* NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS could not be published. Its PackageLicenseExpression named
  'BSD-3-Clause-Attribution', which is neither OSI- nor FSF-approved, and nuget.org accepts
  only approved SPDX ids — rejecting the push AT PUBLISH TIME, after the four sibling
  packages of the same release had already gone out. Verified live:
  licenses.nuget.org/BSD-3-Clause-Attribution -> 404, the full packed expression -> 404, the
  same expression with BSD-3-Clause -> 200. OpenBLAS's own LICENSE is the plain 3-clause BSD,
  so the id was also simply wrong. The expression is now
  'Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause AND (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1)';
  THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt follows suit (and names the current GCC-exception-3.1 id). The csproj
  comment records the pre-flight check so the mistake cannot be re-introduced unnoticed.

  and NumSharp.Interop.pythonnet. It re-packed all four on EVERY `dotnet build` / `dotnet test`
  (the OpenBLAS package re-zipped ~186 MB of bundled runtimes each time, and the pack-time
  "no assets staged" warning fired on every dev build), while CI packs explicitly — build
  -t:Rebuild, then pack --no-build — and even overrode the flag to false in verify-signing to
  dodge the NU5026 it caused there. The pack-time RequireOpenBlasAssets gate is unchanged (it
  is passed to the Pack step, where the check actually runs).

  local-dev default) and no csproj declares Version / PackageVersion / AssemblyVersion /
  FileVersion any more; the SDK derives PackageVersion = Version, AssemblyVersion =

  InformationalVersion = Version+<sha>. That removes the drift the review found — Bitmap's
  4-part 0.60.0.0 beside the others' 0.60.0, and a hard-coded <PackageVersion> next to a
  $(Version)-$(VersionSuffix) conditional, which let a local -p:VersionSuffix=rc.1 pack an
  rc.1 ASSEMBLY inside a non-rc PACKAGE (an explicit PackageVersion is never re-derived).
  Verified: every nupkg packs as 0.60.0 with AssemblyVersion 0.60.0.0, and the

build(ndscope): NumSharp.Build is not contagious - NDW018 refuses to pack it as a dependency

Requirement: a library that references NumSharp.Build gets weaving, but nobody who consumes that
library's package gets weaving - or the weaver.

Measured first (a scripted matrix against the real nupkgs, all consumer shapes):
  - WEAVING never flows. A consumer of a woven library - by ProjectReference or by nupkg - is never
    woven, never imports build/NumSharp.Build.targets, and its own [NDScoped] stays inert. That
    holds even when the library's nuspec DOES list NumSharp.Build: NuGet records the default
    PrivateAssets of `build` as exclude="Build,Analyzers" on the dependency edge, so a transitive
    NumSharp.Build never has its targets imported. The package ships build/ only (never
    buildTransitive/), no lib/, no dependency entries.
  - The DEPENDENCY ENTRY leaked for a hand-written reference. developmentDependency=true only makes
    `dotnet add package` and the VS UI write PrivateAssets="all"; a <PackageReference
    Include="NumSharp.Build"> typed by hand, or under Central Package Management, has no
    PrivateAssets, so `dotnet pack` listed NumSharp.Build as a dependency of the author's package
    (exclude="Build,Analyzers") and every consumer restored the weaver's payload.
  - A package cannot fix that silently: NuGet restores with ExcludeRestorePackageImports=true, so a
    build/NumSharp.Build.props carrying <PackageReference Update="NumSharp.Build"
    PrivateAssets="all"/> never reaches the restore graph, and the pack task takes no

the outcome of that line in the comment beside it (`// nd is now [11. 1. 2. 3.]`, `// (48, 8)`,
`// InvalidOperationException: ...`). Three things shape every script:

  - `dynamic py = host.Namespace` — a PyModule with `import numpy as np` used the pythonnet way:
    `py.x = nd` (the codec runs ToNumpy), `NDArray a = py.x` (AsNDArray when a view is possible),
    `double d = py.v[2]`, `bool b = py.np.shares_memory(py.v, py.c)`, `NDArray r = py.np.sin(py.v / 3.0)`,
    kwargs as C# named arguments, `(long, long) shape = py.np.zeros((2, 3)).shape`. The explicit verbs
    appear where a verb is the subject. Element writes stay `py.Exec("v[0] = 11.0")` (a dynamic
    indexer setter needs a PyObject), multi-index reads `py.Eval("src[1, 2]")` / `a.item(1, 2)`, and

    primitive targets, and numpy.int64 is not a Python int).
  - one `using var scope = NDScope.Open()` per script, opened right after the engine: every NDArray
    built on the thread — slices, transposes, import views — is released when it closes, so no script
    disposes an array by hand; loops open a nested scope per iteration, and a helper that hands an
    array out yields it with `scope.Returns(...)` (06-lifetime shows this meeting the interop's own
    pins and leases).

NoInlining rule, the encoder handoff, sticky process-wide registrations).

Two package changes came out of "test dynamic out":

1. TupleCodec (src/NumSharp.Interop.pythonnet/TupleCodec.cs), registered by RegisterCodec()
   (NumpyCodecOptions.ConvertTuples, default true). pythonnet has no tuple conversion of its own: a
   shape spelled the numpy way through dynamic, `numpy.zeros((2, 3))`, reached numpy as an opaque
   wrapped System.ValueTuple ("expected a sequence of integers or a single integer"), and
   `(long, long) shape = a.shape` could not convert. Encode: any arity (8+ ride the Rest slot),
   nested, mixed, an NDArray element becomes a numpy view through the numpy codec, null becomes
   None. Decode: a Python tuple or subclass (namedtuple, torch.Size) into a C# ValueTuple/Tuple of
   the SAME arity, elements converted by their declared types (an NDArray element through the numpy
   codec, Rest recursively); a length mismatch or a list is declined, never truncated. Probed first:
   pythonnet does route non-primitive dynamic conversions and As<T>() through decoders, so
   `(long, long) s = a.shape` works implicitly; it does NOT consult decoders for long/int/double,
   so numpy scalars cannot be fixed by a codec (hence `.item()`); and `a[1, 2]` cannot bind (the C#
   binder finds no 2-argument indexer on PyObject) — `a.item((1, 2))` and `__setitem__((1, 2), v)`
   do, through the codec. TupleCodecTests (13).

2. EncoderHandoff (src/NumSharp.Interop.pythonnet/EncoderHandoff.cs). Found by the telemetry-ring
   scenario: pythonnet takes its OWN reference from the wrapper an IPyObjectEncoder returns
   (`new NewReference(encoded)`) and never disposes the wrapper, whose reference IS the export pin —
   150 rebindings of one name through `py.win = window` left 150 live exports until a GC plus
   pythonnet's deferred-decref flush, where the explicit `using PyObject p = nd.ToNumpy()` holds one.
   NumpyCodec.TryEncode and TupleCodec.TryEncode now hand their wrapper to a per-thread slot; the
   next encode on that thread disposes the previous wrapper (pythonnet's reference was taken
   synchronously, so it is redundant by then), and DrainPending — the inline housekeeping every
   conversion verb runs — flushes the slot too, so the LAST encode's wrapper does not stay pinned
   until the next encode. Both run under the GIL (Flush takes it re-entrantly). A session counter
   bumped from OnEngineShutdown keeps a stale slot from being decref'd against a dead interpreter.
   Bounded to one wrapper per thread; the finalizer stays the backstop. EncoderHandoffTests (4):
   150 rebindings peak ≤ 2 above baseline, sys.getrefcount shows no lingering wrapper, tuple encodes
   and dynamic call arguments are handed off too. The first cut (dispose only at the next encode)
   made every counter baseline in the suite off by one — the last wrapper lived in the slot forever —
   which is why the flush also lives in DrainPending.

fix(interop/openblas): make the bundled macOS dylib loadable from a NuGet restore (vendored runtime materialized at load) + PackageReference consumer gate in CI

RELEASE BLOCKER. Every NuGet consumer of NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS on macOS got a dylib whose
dependencies were never delivered: dlopen failed with "Library not loaded:
@loader_path/../.dylibs/libgfortran.5.dylib", the backend silently stayed uninstalled, and every
product fell back to the managed kernels while the package claimed byte-parity. CI was green because
every suite consumes the package by ProjectReference, where a csproj Content item copied the very
folder a PackageReference restore never sees.

Root cause, probed (a Mach-O dump of the staged dylibs and a synthetic nupkg restored on this host):
- scipy-openblas' macOS wheel is post-processed by delocate, which parks libgfortran/libquadmath/
  libgcc_s in a .dylibs/ folder BESIDE lib/ and rewrites the main dylib's LC_LOAD_DYLIB entries to
  @loader_path/../.dylibs/<name>. The deps reference each other via @loader_path/<name> and carry the
  placeholder install name /DLC/scipy_openblas64/.dylibs/<name>.
- fetch_openblas.py mirrored that layout (runtimes/<rid>/.dylibs/, a sibling of native/) and the pack
  glob swept it into the nupkg — but NuGet delivers native assets ONLY from under
  runtimes/<rid>/native/. Nested paths are delivered (native/.dylibs/x lands at
  runtimes/<rid>/native/.dylibs/x in the portable layout); a sibling folder extracts to the global
  package cache and is absent from every consumer output. The assets file listed one dylib per macOS RID.
- A RID-specific build/publish additionally FLATTENS nested native assets completely
  (native/.dylibs/x -> <app>/x), so in that layout @loader_path/../.dylibs is the PARENT of the app.
- Two fixes that do not work, verified: pre-loading the deps by absolute path (dyld matches an
  already-loaded image by the requested path or its install name, and the placeholder never matches),
  and relinking with install_name_tool (needs macOS tooling + re-signing on a Linux staging runner,
  and changes the bytes the parity pin hashes).

The fix:

1. Staging + packing (fetch_openblas.py, csproj): the macOS deps are staged and packed NESTED, as
   runtimes/osx-*/native/.dylibs/, which NuGet does deliver. The csproj's current-RID Content item now
   copies the same nested layout to a ProjectReference build's output — deliberately, so the test
   suites hit the exact layout a package consumer gets instead of a sibling copy that hid the bug.
   The manifest (regenerated with --refresh-manifest; every URL and hash of the 8 main libraries is
   unchanged) now pins each vendored file per RID ("vendored": member/file/sha256/size), fetch()
   verifies main + deps and re-stages a tree that is main-only or still carries the pre-fix sibling
   (which it deletes), --check reports an incomplete staging, and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES lists the
   vendored files under their RID.

2. The loader (new MacOsVendoredRuntime.cs + MachOImage.cs; OpenBlasNative.TryLoadCandidates): on
   macOS a candidate that fails to dlopen gets one more chance. MachOImage reads the dylib's load
   commands from the header only (thin 32/64-bit either endian, fat/universal as the union of slices,
   bounded against hostile ncmds/sizeofcmds). MacOsVendoredRuntime plans the closure of missing
   @loader_path/-relative dependencies (sources: <dir>/.dylibs/<name> for the delivered layout, then
   <dir>/<name> for the flattened one; each dep's own @loader_path deps are followed) and materializes
   them where dyld will look:
     - IN PLACE for the runtimes/<rid>/native layout when every target stays inside the RID folder: a
       relative directory symlink runtimes/<rid>/.dylibs -> native/.dylibs, else a per-file copy
       (temp + rename). Nothing is ever written outside the app's own runtimes/ tree; free after the
       first process. The normal outcome for dotnet build / portable publish.
     - A PER-USER CACHE COPY when that folder is read-only or the layout is flattened: main + deps go
       to <cache>/dyld/<sha256 of the main>/native/ + .dylibs/ — the exact relative layout the load
       commands encode — and that copy is what dyld maps. Content-hash keyed (a different binary never
       aliases), every file byte-compared to its source on every hit (a stale/tampered entry is
       rebuilt), a dependency that would escape the entry is refused, writes are temp dir + rename so a
       killed process leaves no half-built entry and two racing processes cannot clobber each other.
       Cache root: NUMSHARP_OPENBLAS_CACHE_DIR (new EnvVars.OpenBlasCacheDir; the buildTransitive props
       now honour the same variable for the build-time cache), else %LOCALAPPDATA% / $XDG_CACHE_HOME /
       ~/.cache + NumSharp/openblas (the build cache's own precedence), else the temp directory.
   Parity-pin story: OpenBlasEngine.LibraryPath keeps naming the file discovery chose — the file
   MatmulParityPin hashes — and the relocated copy is verified identical to it; the new
   OpenBlasEngine.LoadedImagePath reports the file dyld actually mapped, and Info appends
   "(mapped from ...)" when they differ. IsBundledLibrary / the source-marker logic keep working on
   LibraryPath unchanged. Nothing here can throw on the module-initializer path; what happened rides
   in the "tried:" list of a final DllNotFoundException, with dyld's own reason when a retry still fails.

3. The build-time version override (buildTransitive targets) had the same gap on Linux AND macOS: the
   inline task extracted the ONE largest native member, so an override of any non-default version
   staged a main whose content-hashed libgfortran was missing and the required override threw. The
   task now co-extracts every other native member (fetch_openblas.py's vendored_members, same
   relative layout: beside the main on Linux, .dylibs/ on macOS) into the cache entry, describes the
   entry in a .entry.json sidecar ({main, files: {relpath: sha256}}), verifies the main against the
   directory name AND every vendored file against the sidecar on every hit (a pre-sidecar main-only
   entry is discarded as poisoned and re-downloaded), builds the whole entry in a temp sibling renamed
   into place, stages the deps with the main (flattened beside it under FlattenNative, exactly as the
   SDK flattens the bundle), and packs them for OpenBlasDelivery=package.

4. Gates:
   - test/NumSharp.Tests/Backends/OpenBlasMacOsVendoredRuntimeTests.cs (21): the Mach-O reader on
     synthetic thin/big-endian/fat/hostile images and on the real staged dylibs (asserting the nested
     layout and the absence of the sibling); the plan for nested and flattened layouts incl. the deps'
     own deps; in-place materialization (symlink or copy) and its idempotence; completion of a partial
     real sibling; the cache: relocation keyed by content hash, verified hits, rebuild of a tampered
     dep or main, two binaries never aliasing, escape refusal, cache-root precedence; and the
     LoadedImagePath seam. Runs on every OS (the logic is pure path/file work over a parsed header) —
     a macOS-only test would have hidden this exactly like the ProjectReference build did.
   - NEW CI job package-consumer-smoke (windows/ubuntu/macos), a validate-release prerequisite,
     running tools/verify_package_consumer.sh: packs the REAL nupkg (assets required) into a local
     feed, asserts the package shape (every RID under native/, macOS deps nested, no sibling folder,
     Linux deps beside the main), restores it into a scratch consumer BY PACKAGEREFERENCE and proves
     the bundle loads and computes NumPy's answer in the portable layout (macOS: in place, cache
     untouched), from a read-only install (macOS: via the cache, LibraryPath still naming the install's
     file, nothing written into the tree), and from a RID-specific flattened publish (macOS: relocated;
     a tampered cache dep is rebuilt). The job also runs verify_build_override.sh, which never ran in
     CI, so the task's Linux/macOS dep co-staging branch is exercised somewhere; that script's VERSION
     derivation is fixed (it grepped a <Version> the csproj no longer carries and ran with an empty
     version).

Verified on this host: interop + Core + tests build; OpenBlasDeliveryTests + the new tests +
StrongNameTests green on net10.0 and net8.0 (47 each); verify_package_consumer.sh green (win-x64:
shape, PackageReference consumer, flattened publish); verify_build_override.sh 15/15 green with the
reworked cache entry (step 2 discards the pre-sidecar entry and re-downloads, step 3 is a hit, step 10
still self-heals); MatmulParityBackendTests 30/30. The macOS branches themselves (symlink, cache,
flatten) run in the new CI job on macos-latest.

Docs: package README (the vendored runtime + the macOS loader step, NUMSHARP_OPENBLAS_CACHE_DIR,
staged layout, the two scripted gates), the website interop page (bundle section, environment table,

   runtimes/<rid>/native/ folder — so a RID-specific or single-file publish, which flattens the very

1. np.frombuffer(bytes, "float64") threw NotSupportedException — the private dtype-string

     pairwise rule for two arrays — uint8 x int8 must stay float16 (NumPy's ee->e loop), which
     result_type's int16 -> float32 gets wrong; the oracle's arctan2/uint8,int8 cells pin that.

   ("float32"); the NumSharp-only dtypes get lowercase names of their own (char/decimal/str)

fix(interop/openblas): Unix build cache lands in ~/.cache (MSBuild fakes LOCALAPPDATA on Linux/macOS) + the two CI gate scripts compare realpaths and ask MSBuild for the cache

First run of the new package-consumer-smoke job (run 33989137341, on cd2025b3):
  windows-latest  both steps green
  ubuntu-latest   consumer smoke green in EVERY layout (portable, read-only, flattened publish);
                  the override gate died at step 10 with no message
  macos-latest    the bundled dylib LOADED from a PackageReference restore — in place for the
                  portable layout (image == library, bundled=True), through the per-user cache
                  copy for the read-only install (image under the cache, bundled=True, dot00=10) —
                  and then the SCRIPT failed its own path assertion

Two script defects and one real product defect, all reproduced (the Linux one in the official
mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 container against a scratch worktree) before the fix:

1) verify_package_consumer.sh compared the consumer's printed paths against the spelling the
   script created them with. The dotnet host reports realpaths, and on macOS /var is a symlink
   to /private/var, so `library=/private/var/.../ro/...` failed `grep "^library=$RO/"` with
   RO=/var/.... Every path containment check now goes through a realpath helper (`under`).

2) verify_build_override.sh step 10 guessed the build cache as
   ${LOCALAPPDATA:-$HOME/.cache}/NumSharp/openblas and found nothing on Linux — because of (3) —
   and then `find ... | head -1` under `set -o pipefail` plus a captured `dotnet build` left no
   trace of WHY (a failing command substitution under set -e exits silently). The script now
   asks MSBuild where the package's props put the cache (`-getProperty:NumSharpOpenBlasCacheDir`
   on the restored consumer), asserts that on Unix it is ~/.cache/NumSharp/openblas, uses
   `find -print -quit` (no pipeline), and prints the rebuild's output when it fails.

3) The product defect the gate uncovered: MSBuild on Linux/macOS SYNTHESIZES a LOCALAPPDATA
   property (~/.local/share, from SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData) even though no such
   environment variable exists there, so the props' unguarded `$(LOCALAPPDATA)` rule put the
   Unix build cache in ~/.local/share/NumSharp/openblas — while the README, the site page,
   EnvVars.OpenBlasCacheDir and the runtime loader's MacOsVendoredRuntime.ResolveCacheRoot
   (which reads the REAL environment) all say and use ~/.cache/NumSharp/openblas, i.e. the
   "one root for both caches" promise silently did not hold on the two OSes that need the
   runtime cache. The LOCALAPPDATA rule is now guarded with $([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('Windows')),
   so Unix falls through to $XDG_CACHE_HOME, then ~/.cache — the same precedence the runtime uses.
   Probed in the container: NumSharpOpenBlasCacheDir was /root/.local/share/NumSharp/openblas with
   LOCALAPPDATA unset in the environment; it is /root/.cache/NumSharp/openblas after the fix.

Verified: the override gate 15/15 in the Linux container (step 10 now finds and poisons the
entry, sees it discarded and re-downloaded) and 15/15 on Windows in a detached worktree with a
private NuGet cache; the consumer smoke unchanged on Windows.

test(interop/openblas): consumer smoke step 6 makes the cache entry writable before tampering with it

Second run of package-consumer-smoke on macOS (run 33989975903): the bundled dylib now loads from
a PackageReference restore in ALL three layouts — in place through the runtimes/<rid>/.dylibs ->
native/.dylibs symlink for the portable layout, through the per-user cache copy for the read-only
install and for the RID-specific flattened publish, IsBundledLibrary true and dot00=10 everywhere.
Step 6 (tamper a cached dep, expect the loader to rebuild the entry) then exited without a
message: the entry had been populated in step 4 by copying from the read-only install, and
File.Copy on Unix keeps the mode bits, so the cached files were 0444 and the script's own
tamper write was refused (a failed redirection under set -e exits silently). The step now
chmods the entry u+w first and reports both the tamper and the consumer re-run explicitly.
The loader itself never needs write access to an entry's files: it rebuilds an entry by deleting
the directory and renaming a freshly built one into place, which only needs the parent to be
writable.
